one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 holds the Q3 2026 report, expected around Oct 27-28 (not yet confirmed by the company). The company guided Q3 core EPS of $0.85-0.89 and core sales of $4.9-5.0B [1]. Corning usually meets or beats its own guide, but the stock fell after each of the last three reports even on beats: about -5% on Jan 28, -9% on Apr 28 and -12% on Jul 28, 2026, per the price series [13] and [9]. The bar for the Q4 guide, and for progress toward the $20B run-rate target, is high. Supply news since then is positive: a Verizon fiber agreement and an AT&T deal over $3B [5][8]. Against that, the $2B at-the-market sale started in September is an overhang [3][5]. I expect a big move on the report but have no strong view on its sign, with a slight lean negative given the last three reactions. So the median is $155, a touch below spot, at about 20% one-month vol: realized annual vol of ~75% [13] divided by 3.5, plus an earnings-day jump.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: horizon NTM core EPS ~$5.02 x 28x = $141. 40% EV/EBITDA: Oct-2027 TTM EBITDA ~$5.32B x 27x, less ~$5.9B net debt, over ~873M diluted shares = $158. Blend ~$147, about 6% below spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.37 x 1.20. Springboard targets a 19% sales CAGR from Q4'26 to Q4'30 with earnings growing faster [1]. I give no operating-leverage credit on top, because ATM dilution (up to $2B, about 1.4% of shares at $165.96 [3]) and solar losses [1] offset it.

Peer median forward P/E is 29.3x (range 11.8-50.7x). GLW's 2027 EPS growth of +33% ($4.37/$3.29) [11] is close to the peer median of +28%. I set it slightly below the median for three reasons: growth decelerates by the horizon; about 41% of sales come from lower-growth Glass Innovations and Automotive ($1,463M + $471M of $4.74B) [1]; and core EPS includes a +$0.18/qtr hedged-yen adjustment on $0.78 [1].

inputs_detail.derivation: Built from Q2 core EPS growth of +30% and Q3 guide of +28% [1], and 2027 consensus EPS growth of +33% [11]. 4.09 x 1.30 = $5.32B.

Peer median TTM EV/EBITDA is 31.2x (range 11.6-123.5x); GLW trades at 34.7x now [12]. I use 27x, inside the range and below the median: one year on, the peer set's TTM multiples should compress as its hypergrowth slows, and GLW carries a cyclical glass/auto mix.
$6.88B net debt including leases [12], less about $1.0B of assumed ATM proceeds (half of the $2B program [3]).
861.39M outstanding [3] + ~6M ATM shares ($1B / ~$165) + 3M pre-funded warrant [2] + ~2.5M treasury-method dilution from 19.57M options at $139.87 [3] = ~873M

bear.story: AI optical digestion or overbuild scare (the counter-risk Bernstein names [8]; compare the 2001-02 telecom bust, when Corning lost investment grade [10]). 2027 EPS is cut about 15% to ~$3.70. Smartphone and memory pressure hits Glass Innovations [9], solar stays loss-making [1], and the ATM keeps selling into weakness [3]. About 22x a ~$4.0 NTM EPS gives ~$88.

base.story: Corning broadly delivers the ~$4.37 2027 consensus [11] and reaches the $20B run rate by end-2026 [1]. The multiple compresses toward the peer median as growth slows: ~29-30x a ~$5.0 NTM EPS gives ~$150, roughly flat against spot.

bull.story: The NVIDIA and carrier contracts (AT&T >$3B, Verizon) [5][8] pull the $30B Springboard target forward [1]. 2028 EPS reaches $6+ and the market pays ~38x, back near the June highs of ~$255 [13].

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 11.8x (BDC) to 50.7x (LITE). EV/EBITDA 11.6x (BDC) to 123.5x (LITE). The EV/EBITDA figures are TTM, not forward: the source shows no forward EV/EBITDA, so the ev_ebitda_fwd field holds TTM values. Next-year EPS growth median is +28% (range +13% to +75%).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: GLW trades at 42.3x forward P/E [12] (35.9x 2027 consensus) and 34.7x TTM EV/EBITDA, a premium to both peer medians. I apply 28x horizon-NTM P/E and 27x TTM EV/EBITDA, both inside the range and slightly below the medians.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I see no case for a durable premium. GLW's 2027 EPS growth of +33% is near the peer median of +28%, and about 41% of sales come from lower-growth glass and auto [1]. Core EPS depends on a hedged-yen adjustment (+$0.18 of $0.78 in Q2) and a method change on 2026-04-01 that is not recast to prior years [1]. Q2 operating cash flow was flattered by $880M of customer deposits and incentives [1]. The company is issuing equity ($2B ATM plus warrants) rather than buying back stock [2][3]. A small discount fits these facts; a premium has no evidence behind it.

thesis_break_reason: At $98 the stock would trade near 22x 2027 consensus EPS [11], below every AI-optical peer except TEL and BDC, and well under the July 28 panic low of $114.50 [13]. A move there would most likely reflect real 2027 estimate cuts: hyperscaler or carrier order deferrals, fiber price cuts, or the overbuild Bernstein flags [8]. It would not be just a multiple swing.

reasoning: Spot is $156.68, up ~80% in a year after a round trip from $78 to a $271.78 intraday high and back [13]. Realized vol is 74-88% [13]. The fundamentals are strong: core EPS +30%, Q3 guide +28% [1], 2027 consensus $4.37 [11]. But the stock trades at 36x 2027 consensus versus a peer median forward P/E of 29.3x, on similar growth. The skeptic lane turned up six points, all sourced: (1) core EPS includes a +$0.18 hedged-yen adjustment, and the definition changed on 2026-04-01 without recasting prior years [1]; (2) Q2 operating cash flow included $880M of deposits and incentives [1]; (3) the company is issuing equity, with a $2B ATM, a $1B deposit plus a warrant, and a 15M-share warrant at $180 [2][3]; (4) JPMorgan downgraded on valuation and Bernstein is at $140 [7][8]; (5) the stock fell after each of the last three earnings reports [9][13]; (6) Corning has a history of a fiber-capex bust [10]. Against this: no short report surfaced, short interest is only 2.2% of float [12], insider selling is minor (one $1.5M Form 144) [4], and the balance sheet is fine (revolver undrawn, debt $8.4B against $2.5B cash) [1][2]. No current agency rating was found, so none enters the analysis. Fair value is ~$147 (P/E and EV/EBITDA against an 11-name peer set). Scenarios are $88 / $150 / $235 at 25/50/25. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$148 and sigma ~0.58: below realized vol, because vol tends to mean-revert after a spike, but well above the large-cap base rate of 25-35%; I trimmed the far upper tail. Research limits: Twelve Data premium endpoints were unavailable, and some articles were paywalled or blocked, so I did not use them. Because the brief requires an 11-peer comp set, data pages make up most of the source list. Among the research (non-data) sources, 9 of 10 are in lane: filings on dilution, deposits and contingencies, a Form 144, downgrades, a credit history, and selloff coverage.
